blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

Dewdney and Deroche are two separate unincorporated villages on Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) east of Mission, not one town and not inside Mission. The Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) lists Electoral Area G as Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney and Hatzic Island

Deroche's eastern bench ground crosses into Electoral Area C, because the FVRD's Area C plan area runs from the Harrison River to east of Deroche and includes the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench
Corridor streets named on official sources include Lougheed Highway, Taylor Road in Deroche, Hawkins-Pickle Road in Dewdney and North Deroche Road in Deroche
The corridor mixes fee-simple acreage houses with manufactured homes on rented pads, two different ownership types on one page.
Each village has its own elementary school and hall-scale services rather than a shared town centre: Dewdney Elementary at 37151 Hawkins-Pickle Road and Deroche Elementary at 10340 North Deroche Road

blocks.text: Dewdney & Deroche: rules that affect buyers

items.t: FVRD zoning, not City of Mission zoning, governs both villages, under FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021; a Thompson Road parcel in Area G is shown in that bylaw as Agricultural 4 (AG-4), permitting farm and residential use

Norrish Creek, north of Dewdney, is a protected community drinking-water watershed: a provincial assessment states Norrish Creek is a principal water supply for Abbotsford and Mission through the FVRD, with the community intake about 9 kilometres upstream of the Fraser River

blocks.text: Dewdney & Deroche: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Deroche water is billed quarterly on a flat rate: the FVRD's 2026 Area G rates list Water – Deroche at a $102.00 flat rate, with utility bills issued in January, April, July and October

Dewdney water is metered, not flat: FVRD Bylaw No. 1824, 2026 sets the Electoral Area G Dewdney system on a minimum quarterly charge plus per-cubic-metre consumption tiers ( Systems fees and charges amendment BL 1824, 2026.pdf).
The FVRD publishes separate water system maps for Deroche and for the Dewdney Community Water System showing exactly which properties are connected
Area G services named by the FVRD include the Dewdney and Deroche community water systems, North Fraser fire protection, north side street lighting and north side garbage
Nicomen Slough and Deroche Creek both have federal hydrometric stations at Deroche and Dewdney, a sign of how closely water levels on this lowland are monitored

Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) is the only through road, running west to Mission and east toward Harrison Mills and Agassiz, and the proposed BC Transit Highway 7 route would run on it between downtown Mission and downtown Agassiz

blocks.text: Dewdney & Deroche: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood status by parcel identifier number (PID) before valuing a lowland lot, because the Taylor Road and Nicomen Island ground has recorded FVRD freshet evacuation alerts and the Fraser River floodplain covers the corridor floor
Check ALR status by PID on the Agricultural Land Commission maps, because ALR parcels carry the 500 square metre principal-residence limit and the 90 or 186 square metre additional-residence limit
Confirm whether the lot is inside the Deroche or Dewdney water service area on the FVRD system maps, or on a private well and septic system, before assuming community servicing
